prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In a top-down egocentric view looking down at a tiled floor (~1.0–1.5 m away, dark), the camera wearer's own torso and forearms at the bottom are nearest (~0.2–0.5 m, brightest white), holding a nail polish bottle and brush within arm's reach to touch the lower legs and flip-flop-clad feet of a second person seated in front facing the wearer (~0.4–0.8 m away, medium-bright grey, resting on a white towel over the wearer's lap/stool above a blue foot basin). To the upper right (~0.8–1.3 m away, ~0.5 m to the right of the client's left leg), a third person's black-clad lower legs and sneakers extend into the frame from the right, while the upper bodies and heads of all three people remain out of view so it is impossible to see if anyone looks toward the wearer. Across frames 1 to 3 the scene is nearly static with the wearer's left hand slightly occluding the client's left foot, whereas in frames 4 and 5 the wearer leans back and turns clockwise toward the right, making the client's legs retreat toward the upper-left corner as the client lifts their right foot into the blue basin (~0.7–1.0 m) and the wearer's right knee enters the lower-right foreground (~0.3 m). The depth map clearly separates the vertical layering of the wearer's arms, the client's elevated calves and feet, the support cushion below them, and the recessed floor and basin in a way that is harder to gauge from the flat lighting of RGB alone. However, the depth map is unreliable around small details—merging the nail polish bottle, brush, and toe separators into the surrounding hands and feet—and in frame 5 it inaccurately renders the dark trousers of the wearer's right leg and the background floor as a single black void.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to partition the close-up workspace in front of the camera wearer (whose arms and lap sit at ~0.2–0.6 m at the bottom) and the two other people partially visible in the scene: the client facing the wearer with bare lower legs extended from the top (~0.4–0.9 m away, ~0.2 m apart) and a third person's lower legs to the right (~0.8–1.3 m away), though everyone's upper bodies and faces are out of frame. Within the wearer's immediate arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m) are the client's feet in flip-flops with white toe separators, a white towel beneath them, a nail polish bottle and cap in the wearer's hands, and a blue basin just beyond the towel (~0.7–1.0 m). Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera wearer withdraws their hands and rotates rightward in frames 4 and 5, the masks shift from a single large pink `person` region on the left to multiple fragmented masks as the client's right foot moves upward into the basin and the wearer's right leg appears on the lower right. While frame 4 usefully isolates the client's two bare lower legs (light blue `person`) from the wearer's hands, towel, and right arm (pink and brown `person` masks) with sharp boundary contours, the segmentation map is largely unreliable throughout the sequence. It merges the white towel, cushion, and the wearer's arms into the client's `person` mask in frames 1–5, completely misses the third person's legs on the right in frames 2–5, and misclassifies the nail polish cap as a green `remote` in frame 3 and the blue stool edge as a purple `toilet` in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map plots 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background for the camera wearer's hands (~0.3–0.5 m from the camera in the lower foreground) and, in frame 5, a false-positive yellow body skeleton near the client's right foot in the upper-left (~0.7–0.9 m away), while providing no representation of the tiled floor, basin, towel, or the third person's legs ~0.8–1.3 m to the right. In frames 1 to 3, magenta hand skeletons appear at the bottom-left and bottom-center (~0.15 m apart) where the wearer's left hand holds a bottle and the right hand holds a brush within arm's reach of the client's left foot just above them. In frame 4, as the wearer's right hand moves ~0.2 m rightward to hold the side of the client's left foot, only that right hand is tracked, and in frame 5 as the wearer turns rightward, only the wearer's left hand at the bottom-center is detected alongside the erroneous yellow torso/head keypoints superimposed on the client's retreating foot. When detected, the magenta finger joints explicitly show the articulated pinch and curl of the wearer's fingers even where the hands self-occlude or overlap the bottle and foot in RGB. However, the map is highly unreliable: it misses the wearer's right hand in frames 1 and 5 and left hand in frame 4, fails to detect any true leg or foot skeletons for the three partially visible people (whose heads and gaze directions are out of view), and hallucinates a tiny upper-body skeleton on the client's toes in frame 5.
